reading.body:
Equinix's San Jose SV3 facility spans 54,487 square feet with N+1 power and N+2 cooling redundancy, but the operator does not publicly disclose its megawatt capacity.

The absence of published power capacity is notable. Equinix operates the largest retail colocation footprint in Silicon Valley across 12 facilities that collectively serve over 10,500 customers, yet individual facility power specifications remain opaque. This is typical of major operators who treat power allocation as proprietary. For anyone tracking AI infrastructure density and power constraints, the redundancy tier signals reliability architecture but obscures the actual megawatt draw or availability.

Silicon Valley's scale as a colocation hub matters for AI because enterprise and network customers concentrate here. The region's 12-facility footprint suggests distributed power and cooling loads across geography, not centralized bottlenecks. The data does not reveal how much of this capacity serves AI workloads specifically, what percentage runs at utilization, or whether regional power grids are the limiting factor for further expansion. Without megawatt figures from Equinix itself, the building footprint and redundancy design tell only part of the infrastructure story.
